newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Jan 20.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government pays off Ivory Coast's internal debt, apart from cases where the payment is subject to dispute; local government communes and businesses are main beneficiaries; business leaders had criticised delays in promised payments at end of 1996.
- China to supply Ivory Coast with equipment for naval repair yard; equipment paid for by $3 million interest-free loan; protocol signed by visiting Chinese military delegation.
- SOTRA, public transport company in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan, needs 100 extra buses to serve city properly in 1997. This would take the size of the fleet to 813.

- Seminar in central town of Toumodi examines ways of boosting milk production in Ivory Coast; national production of 200,000 tonnes covers just seven percent of domestic needs; imports cost 21.9 billion CFA francs in 1995
- Two policemen implicated in smuggling of 100 kilos of cocaine adding weight to suggestion that Abidjan has become a transit point for illegal drugs from Asia and Latin America.
- African Development Bank gives Ivory Coast a 10 billion CFA loan to improve supplies of drinking water to rural villages
- Ivorian rubber company SOGB holds its annual general meeting in south western port of San Pedro on February 21

- Head of privatised electricity and water utilities Marcel Zadi Kessy reassures workers of soon-to-be privatised state telecommunications company CI-TELCOM; says they need to drop outdated outlooks and adopt a winning mentality.
